questions.q: What is the author's main argument about the Galleri test?
options: It is a proven breakthrough that should replace current screenings
It is promising, but unproven at reducing cancer deaths or advanced cancer
It is so inaccurate that the FDA should reject it outright
It should be restricted to adults under 50 until more trials finish
questions.explain: The author says the test shows promise but has not been shown to lower the risk of death from cancer or prevent advanced cancer.

questions.q: What is the Galleri test's false positive rate?
questions.explain: Only about 0.5% of people, one in every 200, are incorrectly identified as having cancer.

questions.q: What was the test's detection rate for early-stage cancers over three years of screening?
questions.explain: The detection rate for early-stage cancers was only 21%, meaning almost 80% were missed.

questions.q: What is the out-of-pocket cost of the Galleri test currently?
questions.explain: The article states the out-of-pocket cost is currently US$949.

questions.q: What would the author most likely advise someone who decides to get Galleri?
options: Drop mammograms and colonoscopies because Galleri covers over 50 cancers
Pause all routine cancer screening until the FDA announces its decision
Rely on Galleri only for lung and pancreas cancers, skipping other screens
Keep up with recommended screenings for colon, breast, cervical and lung cancers
questions.explain: The author stresses staying current with recommended screenings even if you get the Galleri test.
